title: Change status
purpose: Move an open nonconformance between Open, Investigating, Corrective action and Verification.
summary: Move an open nonconformance to another stage: Open, Investigating, Corrective action or Verification. Closing and reopening have their own forms.

tasks.title: Move the record on
steps: Choose the stage under [[New status]], optionally add [[Reason (optional)]], and select [[Change status]].

tasks.title: Get it ready to close
steps: Then record the check on the record with [[Record effectiveness]].

good_to_know: Any open stage can follow any other. The application does not enforce an order.
Leaving Verification clears the effectiveness check; the history keeps it.
Closed is not a choice here. A supervisor who is not the owner closes the record with Close nonconformance.
Only the owner or a supervisor can change the status.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Opens from Change status on the record, as a dialog or a full page. Only the owner or a supervisor (the admin role included) may open it; anyone else is refused. While the optional nonconformance module is off it answers Not found.

items.label: New status
items.description: Required. The open stages other than the current one: Open, Investigating, Corrective action, Verification. In Verification the field notes Leaving Verification clears the effectiveness check; the history keeps it.

items.label: Reason (optional)
items.description: Kept with the change in the record's history.

items.label: Change status
items.description: Saves and confirms Status changed. The history records Status changed with the status before and after. Leaving Verification also clears the effectiveness result, note and who checked it.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Returns to the record without changing anything.

items.label: Refusals
items.description: The current status: It already has this status. A closed record: A closed nonconformance does not change. A supervisor can reopen it.

items.label: Stale form
items.description: This nonconformance changed after you opened it. Reload it and review the latest details. Your input is kept on the form.

items.label: Signed out by a time limit
items.description: When a time limit signs you out, what you typed here is kept for 24 hours, for you in that browser only, and comes back on this page when you sign in again there (a form open in a dialog opens again on its own page). It keeps the version of the record you typed against: if the record changed since, the page says This record changed after you typed it, and saving is refused with your typing on the form. Copy what you need, then select Discard on the notice, or after a refused save open the form again from the record, to see the record as it stands. It comes back even where the form is no longer offered, for example after the record was closed.
